title: Engine Math Seed Suite
description: Bounded game-development math predicates for agents building or auditing geometry, physics, and engine code. This suite starts with exact integer-coordinate AABB overlap, swept AABB intersection, circle/circle intersection, capsule/circle intersection, circle/AABB intersection, segment intersection, ray/circle intersection, ray/AABB, and point-in-triangle receipts before expanding to harder engine invariants.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Treats collision as a visual guess instead of recording the exact predicate and boundary convention.
tasks.prompt: Do AABB A min(0,0) max(4,4) and AABB B min(3,1) max(6,5) overlap?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only 2D axis-aligned bounding boxes with integer coordinates are checked. Closed intervals are used, so touching edges or corners count as overlap. This is not a swept-collision or physics simulation proof.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Accepts a stated collision result without checking for a separating axis.
tasks.prompt: verify AABB A min(0,0) max(4,4) and AABB B min(5,1) max(7,3) overlap = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite AABB overlap predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate arbitrary collision shapes or runtime engine state.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets to specify whether touching boundaries count as collision, causing off-by-one engine bugs.
tasks.prompt: verify AABB A min(0,0) max(4,4) and AABB B min(4,4) max(6,6) overlap = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-interval convention. A half-open or open-interval engine policy would need a different adapter and receipt.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Uses discrete end-position collision checks and misses the exact time-of-impact window.
tasks.prompt: Do swept AABB A min(0,0) max(1,1) velocity(3,0) intersect AABB B min(3,0) max(4,1) over t in [0,1]?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only one moving 2D AABB against one static 2D AABB with integer velocity over the frame interval 0 <= t <= 1 is checked. This is not a full physics, broad-phase, or response solver proof.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets that already-overlapping boxes at t=0 satisfy a closed continuous-time sweep.
tasks.prompt: verify swept AABB A min(0,0) max(2,2) velocity(5,0) intersect AABB B min(1,1) max(3,3) over t in [0,1] = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-AABB convention. Open-boundary or tolerance-based physics policies need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Claims a collision without checking that the time-of-impact occurs inside the current frame window.
tasks.prompt: verify swept AABB A min(0,0) max(1,1) velocity(1,0) intersect AABB B min(3,0) max(4,1) over t in [0,1] = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite swept AABB predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate arbitrary scenes, collision response, or runtime engine state.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Guesses circular collision visually instead of recording the exact squared-distance predicate and disk convention.
tasks.prompt: Do circle A center(0,0) radius 3 and circle B center(4,0) radius 2 intersect?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only 2D closed disks with integer centers and integer radii are checked. Boundary tangency and containment count as intersection. This is not a manifold, collision-response, or physics-engine proof.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets to specify whether touching circle boundaries count as collision, creating boundary-policy bugs.
tasks.prompt: verify circle A center(0,0) radius 3 and circle B center(5,0) radius 2 intersect = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-disk convention. Open-boundary or tolerance-based physics policies need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Accepts a stated circle collision without checking that the centers are too far apart.
tasks.prompt: verify circle A center(0,0) radius 2 and circle B center(6,0) radius 2 intersect = true
requiredEvidence: distance squared greater than radius-sum squared
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite circle/circle predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate arbitrary collision scenes, swept disks, collision response, or runtime engine state.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Treats character capsule collisions as visual intuition instead of exact closest-point distance predicates.
tasks.prompt: Do capsule A from (0,0) to (4,0) radius 1 and circle B center(2,1) radius 1 intersect?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only one 2D closed capsule with integer segment endpoints and integer radius against one closed disk with integer center and integer radius is checked. This is not a full character controller, swept collision, manifold, or response proof.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets whether capsule boundary tangency counts as a hit, causing off-by-one collision bugs.
tasks.prompt: verify capsule A from (0,0) to (4,0) radius 1 and circle B center(2,2) radius 1 intersect = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-capsule and closed-disk convention. Open-boundary or tolerance-based policies need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Accepts a stated capsule collision without checking the circle center distance to the segment.
tasks.prompt: verify capsule A from (0,0) to (4,0) radius 1 and circle B center(2,4) radius 1 intersect = true
requiredEvidence: distance squared greater than radius-sum squared
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite capsule/circle predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate arbitrary collision scenes, swept capsules, collision response, or runtime engine state.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Uses visual intuition for circle collisions without recording the exact closest-point distance check.
tasks.prompt: Do circle center(2,2) radius 2 intersect AABB min(3,0) max(6,4)?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only 2D circles and AABBs with integer coordinates and integer radius are checked. This is not a swept collision, runtime physics, or rendering proof.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets to define whether circle tangency counts as a collision boundary case.

tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-boundary convention. Open-boundary or tolerance-based collision policies need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Accepts a stated circle collision without checking the squared distance to the nearest AABB point.
tasks.prompt: verify circle center(0,0) radius 2 intersect AABB min(3,3) max(5,5) = true
requiredEvidence: distance squared greater than radius squared
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite circle/AABB predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate arbitrary collision scenes or runtime engine state.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Guesses that two debug/editor line segments cross without preserving orientation evidence.
tasks.prompt: Do segment A from (0,0) to (4,4) and segment B from (0,4) to (4,0) intersect?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only non-degenerate 2D line segments with integer coordinates are checked. This does not verify arbitrary curve, mesh, or physics-engine collision behavior.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Sees collinearity and forgets to check closed segment bounds before claiming intersection.
tasks.prompt: verify segment A from (0,0) to (1,1) and segment B from (2,2) to (3,3) intersect = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite segment-intersection predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate runtime engine state or broader geometry scenes.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Misses boundary-policy details for collinear overlapping line segments.
tasks.prompt: verify segment A from (0,0) to (4,0) and segment B from (2,0) to (6,0) intersect = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-segment convention. Open-segment or tolerance-based policies need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Uses raycast intuition without preserving the exact closest-point distance predicate.
tasks.prompt: Do ray origin(0,0) direction(1,0) intersect circle center(3,1) radius 2?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only one 2D ray with integer origin and nonzero integer direction against one closed disk with integer center and integer radius is checked. This is not a full raycaster, visibility, BVH, rendering, or physics proof.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets to define whether ray tangency against a circle counts as a hit.
tasks.prompt: verify ray origin(0,0) direction(1,0) intersect circle center(3,2) radius 2 = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded closed-disk and t >= 0 ray-domain convention. Open-boundary or segment-limited raycasts need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Checks the infinite line against the circle but forgets that the ray only exists for t >= 0.
tasks.prompt: verify ray origin(0,0) direction(1,0) intersect circle center(-3,0) radius 1 = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite ray/circle predicate is refuted. The receipt does not evaluate arbitrary raycast systems, acceleration structures, visibility, or runtime engine state.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Uses floating-point intuition for ray hits without preserving the exact t interval.
tasks.prompt: Do ray origin(0,2) direction(1,0) intersect AABB min(3,0) max(5,4)?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only 2D rays with integer origin/direction and integer-coordinate AABBs are checked. The receipt does not verify full raycaster, BVH, rendering, or physics-engine behavior.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Forgets that a ray parallel to a slab must be inside that slab to hit the box.
tasks.prompt: verify ray origin(0,5) direction(1,0) intersect AABB min(3,0) max(5,4) = true
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only the stated finite ray/AABB predicate is refuted. This does not evaluate arbitrary scene geometry.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Checks the infinite line against the box but forgets the ray domain t >= 0.
tasks.prompt: verify ray origin(6,2) direction(1,0) intersect AABB min(3,0) max(5,4) = false
tasks.checkerBoundary: The result depends on the recorded ray-domain convention. Infinite-line or segment-cast checks need separate adapters and receipts.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Uses a sketch or floating-point intuition for triangle picking without preserving exact edge tests.
tasks.prompt: Is point (1,1) in triangle A(0,0) B(4,0) C(0,4)?
tasks.checkerBoundary: Only non-degenerate 2D triangles and points with integer coordinates are checked. This does not verify arbitrary mesh, rasterizer, or collision-engine behavior.

tasks.aiFailureMode: Accepts a visual triangle-membership claim without checking all three oriented edges.
